lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Why the tears, Tantalus? What are you standing by the lake lamenting yourself for?

lines.speaker: Tantalus
lines.text: Because, Menippus, I'm dying of thirst.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Are you really so lazy you can't bend down and drink? Or, for that matter, scoop some up in your cupped hand?

lines.speaker: Tantalus
lines.text: No use bending down. The water runs away the moment it senses me coming. And if I do manage to scoop some and bring it to my mouth — I haven't even wet the edge of my lip before it slips through my fingers, somehow, and leaves my hand dry again.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: That is a remarkable condition, Tantalus. [pause] But tell me — what do you need a drink for, exactly? You don't have a body. That's buried somewhere back in Lydia — the thing that could feel hunger and thirst. You're a soul. How could a soul still get thirsty? Or drink, for that matter?

lines.speaker: Tantalus
lines.text: That's precisely the punishment — that the soul thirsts as though it were a body.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: All right, we'll take your word for it, since you say the thirst is your sentence. But — what's actually so terrible about it? Are you afraid you'll die for lack of a drink? [pause] I don't see another underworld after this one, or another death to take you somewhere else.

lines.speaker: Tantalus
lines.text: Quite right. And that's part of the sentence too — wanting to drink when there's no need.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: You're talking nonsense, Tantalus. Honestly, you do sound like a man who needs a drink — of neat hellebore, by Zeus. You've got the opposite problem of people bitten by mad dogs: you're not afraid of the water, you're afraid of the thirst.

lines.speaker: Tantalus
lines.text: I wouldn't refuse the hellebore either, Menippus. Just let me have something.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Don't worry, Tantalus — neither you nor any other corpse is going to drink. It can't be done. [pause] Though admittedly, not everyone has your problem: most of them aren't under sentence to be thirsty while the water shrinks away.
